subject: Access activation protocols and rollback lane
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
To: Jill Park <jill.park@acmetech.com>, ops@acmetech.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Access activation protocols and rollback lane

Hi Jill / Acme ops team,

Thanks again for the sync yesterday. To make the activation window smooth next week we want to confirm the exact protocols and a clear rollback lane in case anything needs to be reverted quickly. Summary of what we need from you before the kickoff: 

- SAML metadata (IdP metadata XML) for your staging environment (entityID, ACS URL, certificate). We attached a sample XML schema for reference.
- SCIM provisioning window you prefer (UTC) and whether you want incremental provisioning or full-sync on day zero.
- IP allowlist ranges (CIDRs) for your egress to Redwood Dedicated; please include both staging and prod ranges.
- Service account ownership & minimum roles for the integration (who will manage tokens/keys).
- Any org policies (e.g., disallow external sharing, session timeout limits) that would block tooling we use for onboarding.

Proposed activation timeline (high level):
1) Monday 06:00-08:00 UTC – staged SSO test, validate auth flows, and verify SCIM create/patch flows.
2) Monday 08:30-09:30 UTC – broaden SCIM sync and run smoke jobs.
3) Monday 10:00-11:00 UTC – promote to prod toggles if all checks green.

Rollback lane: if auth failures or user deprovisioning regressions occur, we will revert the configuration to the previous SAML metadata and disable SCIM push for 30 minutes while we triage. To make that safe we need a named contact who can approve the revert within 15 minutes.

Attachments: saml-config-example.xml, ip-allowlist.csv, mutual-action-plan.xlsx (MAP).

Can you confirm the staging IdP metadata and preferred SCIM window by EOD today so Ben can draft the service-account role map? Also flag the revert approver you want on-call for the window.

Thanks,
Maya
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Access activation protocols and rollback lane

Maya / team,

Thanks — attaching our staging IdP metadata (saml-config-example.xml) and a quick CSV with the staging + prod IPs (ip-allowlist.csv). A few notes: 

- Staging IdP uses entityID: https://idp.staging.acmetech.com and ACS URL https://staging.redwood.acme/saml/acs. Cert included in the XML.
- For SCIM, we prefer an incremental provisioning window: daily delta at 07:00 UTC for production; for the cutover we can do a full sync in staging at 06:30 UTC and a delta for prod at 09:00 UTC.
- Our security team requires that any service account used for provisioning is restricted to "scim:users.write" and "scim:groups.read" only. They won't allow broader admin scopes.

Rollback approver: Ops on-call (ops@acmetech.com) will be the primary revert approver during the activation window; secondary is myself.

One constraint: our firewall team needs at least 48 hours to add new IPs to the prod allowlist. The prod ranges in the CSV are already requested but may not be live until Monday 08:00 UTC. If they are not live at 08:30 UTC we'll need to run the smoke tests over a short VPN tunnel we can open.

On the attach: saml-config-example.xml (IdP metadata), ip-allowlist.csv (CIDRs).

Cheers,
Jill Park
Director, Identity & Access
AcmeTech

Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access activation protocols and rollback lane

Thanks Jill — this is helpful. Quick implementation notes from the ops side: 

- Service accounts & least privilege: we will create two namespaced service accounts on our side: 
  * redwood-scim-staging (scim:users.write, scim:groups.read) — used only during staged sync and deleted after validation unless you want long-lived tokens.
  * redwood-scim-prod (scim:users.write) — token stored in your KMS; rotate after first 30 days.

- Activation checklist (technical):
  1) Validate IdP metadata in staging (certificate chain and claim mappings).
  2) Run SCIM full-sync in staging with sample users (10 test users).
  3) Confirm IP allowlist is active for staging. If prod ranges are not live we will run prod smoke through the VPN tunnel Jill mentioned and keep the revokable toggle ready.
  4) Run login smoke and token refresh tests for 15 minutes; collect logs and token traces.
  5) Flip prod toggle -> monitor for 30 min; if any user deprovisions unexpectedly revert to previous metadata & pause SCIM pushes.

- Rollback procedure (short):
  * Step 0: Halt SCIM pushes (disable service account token).
  * Step 1: Revert to previous IdP metadata (we keep the prior copy in the staging bucket).
  * Step 2: Re-run sanity logins for 5 key accounts.
  * Step 3: Re-enable SCIM in monitored mode and run a limited patch to test.

I will prepare a one-page runbook and put it in the MAP (mutual-action-plan.xlsx) with explicit toggles and the revert approver email lined up. Two asks to Acme: please confirm ops@acmetech.com as the real-time revert approver and let us know if your firewall team can prioritize the CIDR change before 08:00 UTC on Monday.

If everything looks good I can be on the activation call Monday and own the runbook execution.

Ben Carter
Implementation Lead, Customer Success Ops
Redwood Inference
